solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tech company with power that is a US symbol

indicators.note: 'with' simply sets one part alongside the next, so the pieces join in sequence

blocks.note: Apple is the computer and phone maker
P is the physics symbol for power
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation id est, meaning that is

explanation.surface: A tech giant boasting that its power has made it an emblem of America.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'that is a US symbol' as a clause, but 'that is' is the abbreviation i.e. and the definition is only 'a US symbol'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'as American as apple pie' makes this dessert a proverbial emblem of the United States.

clue.text: Commercial separation, having no purpose

blocks.note: an ad is a commercial on TV or radio
a rift is a split or separation

explanation.surface: A business split that leaves everyone wondering what the point is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commercial' looks like an adjective qualifying 'separation', but it is the noun meaning an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone drifting without aim or direction in life is figuratively described as being cast loose at sea.

clue.text: Friend having top that’s rather washed out

indicators.note: one thing having another means it comes with the other attached, so the parts join up

blocks.note: a pal is a friend
a lid is the top of a jar or box

explanation.surface: A friend wearing a top whose colour has faded in the wash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' suggests a garment, which suits 'washed out', but here it is a cover for a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Pallid is a synonym for pale or wan, describing a complexion or colour lacking in vividness.

clue.text: Sad verse excited glee, with unknown ending

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so these letters are agitated into a new order
'with' attaches one part to another so they are joined in sequence

blocks.note: taken as written
y is a mathematical unknown, placed here as the ending

explanation.surface: A melancholy poem somehow stirs up great joy, though how it finishes is a mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: In algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns, so crosswords use any of them for 'unknown'; 'ending' tells you where it goes.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a mournful poem, typically a lament for the dead, so it is sorrowful poetry.

clue.text: Country store?

blocks.note: first meaning: the island nation in the North Atlantic
second meaning: a British supermarket chain known for frozen food

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a village shop out in the countryside; instead it is a nation and also the name of a British frozen-food supermarket chain.
explanation.definitionFit: The same name belongs to a Nordic island republic and to a well-known UK grocery retailer of frozen goods.

clue.text: Reconstruct flue with us? That’ll be handy

indicators.note: to reconstruct is to rebuild in a new form, so the letters are put together differently

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, 'with' adding it to the other fodder

explanation.surface: A builder offers to rebuild a chimney flue together; that would come in handy.
explanation.walkthrough: A flue is a chimney duct, which makes 'reconstruct' sound like building work.
explanation.definitionFit: Handy and useful are synonyms, both describing something convenient and of practical help.

clue.text: Sally has account with debts – it’s obscene

indicators.note: one thing that has another carries it along next to it, so the parts join
'with' adds a further part to the end of the sequence

blocks.note: the pet name formed by cutting the name short, dropping its last two letters
AC is the abbreviation for account
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: Sally's account is so deep in debt that it is positively indecent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' is a woman's name shortened to SAL, not a sortie or witty remark; an IOU is a note saying 'I owe you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Salacious describes lewd, indecent material, so it works as a synonym for the stronger word.

clue.text: The best method of working in wooded area

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a forest is a large wooded area
MO is modus operandi, Latin for a method of working

explanation.surface: Advice on the finest technique for working among trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The best method of working' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'The best'; modus operandi is shortened to MO.
explanation.definitionFit: Foremost means leading or most prominent, so it equals being top of the rank above all others.

clue.text: Len’s dice playing is officially permitted

indicators.note: playing means moving about freely, so the letters tumble into another order

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: Len has a gambling permit, so his game of dice is legal.
explanation.walkthrough: The dice game is a fitting picture for a gambling licence, but 'playing' is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Something licensed has been granted formal authorisation, like a pub allowed to sell alcohol.

clue.text: Re-experienced swallowing ecstasy, free of anxiety now

indicators.note: to swallow something is to take it inside, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: to relive something is to experience it again
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone who relived a trip after taking a pill now feels calm again.
explanation.walkthrough: Ecstasy suggests a feeling, which fits the calm ending, but it is the drug, abbreviated E.
explanation.definitionFit: Being relieved means feeling reassured once a worry or fear has passed, so no longer anxious.

clue.text: Caught student with Ernie’s partner, a priest

indicators.note: 'with' adds the next part on, so the pieces join in sequence

blocks.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
L is a learner, from the British learner-driver plate
Eric Morecambe was the comedy partner of Ernie Wise

explanation.surface: A student is caught with the friend of someone called Ernie, who turns out to be a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe and Wise, Eric and Ernie, were a hugely popular British TV comedy double act.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleric is a member of the clergy, so a priest is one example of the general term.

clue.text: Spanish car: you may sit in it

blocks.note: first meaning: the Spanish car manufacturer
second meaning: a chair or place to sit

explanation.walkthrough: The second half sounds like a comment about the car's interior, but it is a separate everyday meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The Barcelona carmaker shares its name with the common noun for anything you sit on.

clue.text: Fat lady, losing daughter, explodes with ire: what a story!

indicators.note: to lose something is to be without it, so a letter is dropped
'with' adds a further part to the letters already gathered
an explosion scatters everything, so the letters fly into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
d is the abbreviation for daughter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A large woman whose daughter has left her flies into a rage, and the onlooker marvels at the tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation 'what a story!' is the definition, said of an unlikely tale; the anagram uses the remaining letters of the lady plus the anger.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy tale is a far-fetched story or fabrication, the kind that prompts the exclamation of disbelief.

clue.text: Food ingredient using copper and trimmed herb

indicators.note: 'and' adds one part to another so they join in sequence
trimming cuts off an edge, so the final letter is removed

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
mint is a common herb

explanation.surface: A recipe ingredient prepared in a copper pan with some chopped herbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trimmed herb' sounds like kitchen prep, but it means cutting the last letter off a herb's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cumin is a seed spice widely used in cooking, so it is a culinary component in many dishes.

clue.text: Fifty plus acres, perhaps?

blocks.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
and means plus, as in two and two

explanation.surface: Someone guesses a plot runs to more than fifty acres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fifty plus' reads as an estimate of size, but it is a Roman numeral followed by a word meaning plus; 'perhaps' marks acres as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Acres are a measure of ground area, so a stretch of territory is what they quantify.

clue.text: Smartphone program to get a lake fish is dreadful

blocks.note: an app is a program on a phone
taken as written
L is the map abbreviation for lake
the ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A phone app for buying fish from a lake turns out to be terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: Ling is a favourite crossword fish; 'lake' is shortened to its map abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Appalling and dreadful are synonyms, both describing something shockingly bad or of very poor quality.

clue.text: Sounds horn with one end of toe and foot, childishly

indicators.note: 'with' adds the following parts on in sequence
the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: a driver toots a horn
I is the Roman numeral for one
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A horn honks as someone stubs a toe and a foot, described in baby talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toe and foot' look paired, but 'and' joins wordplay to the definition 'foot, childishly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tootsie is a playful nursery word for a little foot or toe, used when talking to small children.

clue.text: Guess teatimes varied

indicators.note: varied means changed around, so the letters take a different arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone invited to work out when tea is served, since the hour changes.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words have the same eight letters, so the whole answer comes from the meal times rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to make an approximate judgement, so the noun or verb matches a rough guess.

clue.text: Come across lazy type with horse

indicators.note: 'with' sets one part beside the next so they join in sequence

blocks.note: a bum is an idle loafer
a pinto is a piebald or skewbald horse

explanation.surface: Meeting an idler who has his horse in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinto, a horse with patchy colouring, is a handy horse name in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To bump into someone is an idiom for meeting them by chance, the same as encountering them.

clue.text: Plums cooked by Mr Davey, sitting heavily

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are mixed into a new order
'by' means next to, so one part is placed beside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
Ed Davey, leader of the UK Liberal Democrats

explanation.surface: A politician, stuffed after eating stewed plums, sprawls in his chair.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Ed Davey is the leader of Britain's Liberal Democrat party, which supplies the first name.
explanation.definitionFit: To be slumped is to have collapsed into a chair in a heavy, drooping posture.

clue.text: Outspoken medic in courtroom area

indicators.note: outspoken literally means spoken out, so the word is said rather than spelt

blocks.note: doc is a casual word for a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor speaking frankly while on trial in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outspoken' looks like a description of a candid medic, but it signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The dock is the enclosure in a criminal court where the defendant stands during a trial.

clue.text: President in vehicle reaching middle of nowhere

indicators.note: reaching means arriving next to, so one part runs up against the other
the middle of a word is its centre letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: a bus is a road vehicle
the centre letter of the seven-letter word

explanation.surface: A head of state being driven deep into the back of beyond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the link word: the president is the definition, not a piece placed inside the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bush and his son George W. Bush were both US presidents, so the surname fits.

clue.text: Ban lace pants to create stability

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are judged a mess to be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A proposal to outlaw lacy underwear in the interest of steadiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lace pants' reads as lingerie; in British slang 'pants' also means rubbish or nonsense, which signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Balance means equilibrium or steadiness, the state of being stable rather than tipping over.

clue.text: After a long time, regularly trimmed unideal schedule

indicators.note: 'After' fixes the order, so the later part follows the earlier one
trimming at regular intervals cuts every other letter, leaving the alternate ones

blocks.note: an age is a long time
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: After ages of delay, a flawed timetable is cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the trimmed word after the long time, so the age comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is the list of items to be dealt with at a meeting, a plan or programme.

clue.text: Interfere in award, one hears

indicators.note: what one hears is how a word sounds, not how it is written

blocks.note: a medal is an award

explanation.surface: Someone is rumoured to have tampered with a prize decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interfere in' looks like a single phrasal verb, but 'in' is the link word joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To meddle is to intrude in affairs that are not your concern, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Drive forward as part of grim peloton

indicators.note: being part of something means sitting within it, so the letters run inside the words

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A cyclist pushes ahead within a grimly determined pack of riders.
explanation.walkthrough: A peloton is the main bunch of riders in a cycle race, which makes 'drive forward' look like racing jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to propel or urge onwards, applying force that pushes something ahead.

clue.text: Pass by group to see workmate

indicators.note: 'by' means beside, so one part sits next to the other

blocks.note: a col is a mountain pass
a league is an association or group

explanation.surface: Someone walks past a crowd of people to visit a fellow employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass by' looks like a phrasal verb, but 'pass' is a noun, the mountain gap, and 'by' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A colleague is a fellow member of staff, so a co-worker or associate in the same job.

clue.text: Steer clear of sinner receiving promotion

indicators.note: to receive is to take in, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: Eve, who ate the forbidden fruit, is the first sinner
an ad is a promotion or advertisement

explanation.surface: Avoid a wrongdoer who has just been promoted at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Promotion' suggests a step up at work, but here it is an advertisement; Eve is the classic crossword sinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to avoid or dodge something, keeping away from it deliberately.

clue.text: A free BBC

blocks.note: taken as written
to untie is to set free

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a slogan for a free broadcaster, but 'free' is a verb meaning release from bonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Auntie, or Auntie Beeb, is the long-standing affectionate British nickname for the national public broadcaster.

clue.text: Queen once hosted by a French doctor without staff

indicators.note: a guest hosted by someone is held within their home, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: Queen Anne reigned in the early eighteenth century
un is French for a
MD is Doctor of Medicine

explanation.surface: A former monarch stays with a French physician who has no servants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks a past queen; 'a French' means the French word for 'a', and the queen sits inside the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmanned describes a place or machine that has no crew or personnel operating it.

clue.text: Brian from Roxy Music? Yuk! Too much!

blocks.note: Brian Eno was a founding member of the band Roxy Music
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: A listener reacts to a Brian Eno record with disgust and begs for it to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the final exclamation, which reads like a continuation of the disgusted reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouting 'Enough!' is a way of saying you can take no more, the same protest as an overload.

clue.text: Create concoction of green tea

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so these letters are blended into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to brew up a mixture involving green tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concoction' fits the drink, but it means the letters of the tea are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: To generate is to produce or bring into being, a synonym for making something new.
